instruction: Use Abaqus to perform a transient heat-transfer analysis of a rectangular solid block (Variant A). Use the N-mm-MPa unit system with appropriate thermal units. Model Definition: Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Extrusion. Sketch a rectangle from (0, 0) to (60, 18) and extrude it by 12 mm to produce a block of size 60 mm x 18 mm x 12 mm. Material and Section: Define a material named Steel with density = 7.85e-9 tonne/mm^3, thermal conductivity = 0.045 W/(mm·K), and specific heat = 4.5e8 mJ/(tonne·K). Create a Homogeneous Solid Section using Steel and assign it to the entire block. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the block. Analysis Step: Create a Heat Transfer step named Step-Heat-A with transient response. Set the time period to 300 s, the initial increment to 2 s, the maximum increment to 15 s, and the maximum allowable temperature change per increment DELTMX to 10. Initial and Boundary Conditions: Apply an initial uniform temperature of 25 degC to the whole block. Apply a temperature boundary condition of 95 degC on the X = 0 face during Step-Heat-A. Discretization: Mesh the block with a global seed size of 4 mm. Assign DC3D8 heat-transfer brick elements and generate the mesh. Job Execution: Create a job named Job-TransientHeat-A, submit it for analysis, and wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Post-Processing: Review the temperature field at the final time. Record the average temperature near the X = 0 heated face, the average temperature in the X approximately 5 mm band, and the final analysis time. Deliverables: Save the model database as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-TransientHeat-A.cae and ensure the output database is written to C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-TransientHeat-A.odb. Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated.
